facts.fact: TV advertising spend is on track to grow past $150 billion by 2032, according to the page.
facts.quote: TV advertising spend is on track to grow past **$150 billion by 2032**, proving its lasting value.

facts.fact: The page states that 80% of advertisers now use Connected TV (CTV) to target specific households.
facts.quote: with **80% of advertisers** now using it to target specific households

facts.fact: The page states that TV often delivers a return on investment four times higher than many digital ads.
facts.quote: TV often delivers a return on investment that's **four times higher** than many digital ads

facts.fact: The page states that commercials triggering feelings like happiness or surprise can boost brand recall by up to 30% compared to emotionally neutral ads.
facts.quote: Commercials that trigger feelings like happiness or surprise can boost brand recall by up to **30%** compared to ads that are emotionally neutral.

facts.fact: The page states that 60% of viewers say TV ads influence their buying decisions.
facts.quote: With **60%** of viewers saying TV ads influence their buying decisions

facts.fact: The page advises building a TV commercial around a story viewers can follow in 30 seconds.
facts.quote: Build the commercial around a story viewers can follow in 30 seconds.

facts.fact: The page says viewers have maybe five seconds to capture attention with the opening hook.
facts.quote: You have maybe five seconds, tops.

facts.fact: The page describes the production breakdown sheet as having three core rows: Script, Video, and Audio.
facts.quote: The production structure typically uses a breakdown sheet with three core rows: Script (narrative actions), Video (shot compositions), and Audio (music and sound effects).

facts.fact: The page says the three-act structure for a 30-second spot is Setup, Conflict, and Resolution.
facts.quote: Every great story, from Hollywood blockbusters to 30-second ads, follows the classic three-act structure.

facts.fact: Gross Rating Points (GRPs) are described on the page as the industry standard for measuring the total size of the audience a media placement reaches, calculated as Reach x Frequency.
facts.quote: Gross Rating Points are the industry standard for measuring the total size of the audience you're hitting. It’s basically **Reach x Frequency**

facts.fact: Frequency is defined on the page as the average number of times a person or household sees a given ad over a set period.
facts.quote: This one tracks the _average_ number of times a person or household sees your ad over a set period.

facts.fact: Connected TV (CTV) is defined on the page as any content streamed through a smart TV, gaming console, or device such as Roku or Apple TV.
facts.quote: This is any content streamed through a smart TV, a gaming console, or a device like a Roku or Apple TV.

facts.fact: Addressable TV is defined on the page as technology that shows different ads to different households watching the same cable or satellite program.
facts.quote: It allows different ads to be shown to different households even if they're watching the _exact same program_ on cable or satellite.

facts.fact: The page describes call-tracking services as able to generate a unique phone number for a single commercial so that every call from that ad can be counted.
facts.quote: Services that provide call-tracking can generate a unique phone number just for your ad.

facts.fact: The page describes color grading as the post-production process that fine-tunes a commercial's colors to create a consistent and visually appealing look.
facts.quote: This process fine-tunes the colors to create a consistent and visually appealing look.

facts.fact: According to the page, producing a TV commercial can cost from a few thousand dollars for a simple local spot to hundreds of thousands of dollars for a national ad with celebrity talent and special effects.
facts.value: a few thousand dollars to hundreds of thousands
facts.quote: The cost to produce a TV commercial can swing wildly from a few thousand dollars for a simple, local spot to hundreds of thousands for a glossy national ad

facts.fact: The page states that TV ads are typically produced in 15-second, 30-second, and 60-second formats.
facts.quote: You’ll typically see ads in **15**, **30**, and **60-second** formats

facts.fact: The page's FAQ states that 30 seconds is the standard and most effective length for a TV commercial.
facts.quote: 30 seconds is the standard and most effective length.

facts.fact: The page says response attribution is visible as a website traffic jump in the minutes right after a commercial is scheduled to air.
facts.quote: Watch your website analytics closely in the minutes right after your commercial is scheduled to air.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its AI platform takes users from a simple idea to a finished ad in minutes, versus the weeks or months traditional production takes.
facts.quote: taking you from a simple idea to a finished ad in minutes.

facts.fact: The page claims AI models are trained on thousands of successful commercials.
facts.quote: AI models are trained on thousands of successful commercials
